plumbing.summary: Everything passed: gofmt, go vet, the tests of every package the change touches, and every acceptance test.
plumbing.review:
One merge prerequisite remains: **record and cite the private-retention decision**. [SPEC.md:136](SPEC.md:136) leaves this as an instruction to the merger; no corresponding decision is recorded. [D-0116:1](D-0116.jsonl:1) still says commands are never retained. This is the merger’s responsibility, since the build cannot write `decisions/`.

Otherwise, I found no blocking implementation defect:

- Changes stay within the ratified files and implement explicit run selection, bounded command retention, private opt-in, and display clearing.
- Acceptance sources match the plan exactly. Assertions exercise actual behavior; I found no weakening or production special-casing.
- Access checks precede private serialization; public caches remain command-free. Commands render through `textContent`. No unplanned host/network access or secret disclosure was introduced.
- Naming, comments, and idioms fit the surrounding code.

Verification limitation: I relied on the factory’s passing results rather than rerunning write-producing tests. The [page acceptance test:15](act_shell_page_accept_test.go:15) explicitly covers initial HTML only; browser clearing and late-response behavior were reviewed statically.

VERDICT: changes needed — the merger must record the D-0116 private-retention/display exception and cite its decision ID in SPEC.md.
